Optimiser settings for ctFit

Source: R/ctOptimControl.R
ctOptimControl.Rd

The settings ctFit reads from optimcontrol. Each has the same meaning on both backends. A setting the backend does not have is an error, unless its value asks for what that backend does anyway (gradient = 'adjoint' on stan, nsubsets = 1 on julia), and so is a misspelled name. Settings left unset take the backend's default.

Stopping

tol

Both. Stop when the objective changes by less than this. Default 1e-8 on stan, off on julia.

g_tol

Both. Stop when the l2 norm of the gradient falls below this. Default 1e-8 on julia, off on stan.

x_tol

Both. Stop when the parameter step falls below this. Off by default.

maxiter

Both. Iteration cap. Default 1000 on julia, mize's on stan.

lbfgs_scores

Julia. Default TRUE. Keeps a second model of the curvature beside L-BFGS, built from the outer product of the subjects' scores, and takes each step with whichever model predicted the last step better.

lbfgs_local

Julia. Default TRUE. With intoverpop = 'laplace', parameters that only a few subjects or groups inform (a study's, a group's, or an item few answered) start L-BFGS from their exact curvature, computed from those subjects alone.

lbfgs_memory

Both. How many curvature pairs L-BFGS keeps. Default on julia one per free parameter, between 20 and 1000, and mize's default on stan.

stallretries

Both. Default 2. How many times a fit that stopped short of a maximum is continued. Stan restarts from new random values when the gradient exceeds stalltol per data point. Julia resumes from a better point found by its end-of-fit checks, or from where it stopped, and keeps the resumed run only if it improves the objective. 0 turns it off.

Starting values

initsd

Both. Default 0.01. The sd of the random start, on the raw scale.

datastart

Julia. Default TRUE. Starting values for the diagonals of DRIFT, DIFFUSION, T0VAR and MANIFESTVAR are set from the scale of the data, using log(1 + y) for counts, and without using binary or ordinal indicators. If the objective cannot be evaluated there, the fit starts from the default values and says so. Supplied inits are always used as given.

flatretry

Julia. Default FALSE. When the optimiser leaves a parameter far out where the likelihood hardly changes with it, such as an auto-effect so fast or so slow that its value no longer matters, or a variance or random effect standard deviation at zero, TRUE optimises again from the starting values with that parameter held at the other side of its range, then lets it go. The better of the two results is kept. This happens before the standard errors are computed, and costs up to two more optimisations for each such parameter. With FALSE the fit names such parameters in a message, and ctFitFlatRetry does the same for a fit afterwards.

carefulfit

Both. Default TRUE. A first pass with ctsem's normal(0,1) priors on every raw parameter, to find starting values, after which the fit's own objective is maximised. Skipped with priors = TRUE, which has those priors already, and when inits are supplied. On julia it runs until it converges, for at most 200 iterations, and a number sets that limit. It keeps a fit from starting at a boundary, such as a correlation of one or a variance of zero. fit$optim$carefulfit records whether it ran.

The optimiser

stochastic

Both. Start with ctsem's stochastic-gradient optimiser and finish with L-BFGS. 'auto' does so above 50 parameters. Default TRUE on stan, FALSE on julia. It can be much faster than L-BFGS alone on large, poorly conditioned models, and can also take a fit further toward a degenerate limit, such as a variance going to zero. fit$optim$sgd_iterations records it.

gradient

Julia. 'adjoint' (reverse mode, the default) or 'forward'. Both give the same gradient, and the cost of the adjoint does not grow with the number of parameters.

batch

Julia. Default TRUE, or FALSE when inits are supplied. Start on a random subset of the subjects and add more as the fit needs them. Needs at least 80 subjects or top-level groups. TRUE also batches a fit started from supplied inits.

coreset

Julia. Default 'auto'. Run parts of the optimisation on a weighted subset of the subjects (or of the top-level groups, with intoverpop = 'laplace'), chosen to reproduce the full gradient, and check each part against the full gradient. The fit finishes on all the data, so the estimates and standard errors use every subject. 'auto' uses subsets for data with at least 200 subjects or top-level groups and 10,000 data cells (rows times manifest variables). On smaller data they save no time, and can change which of several maxima a fit reaches. TRUE uses them whenever they are expected to save gradients, FALSE never. fit$optim$coreset_sizes records them.

explosive_forward

Julia. Default FALSE. For a subject whose predictions grow more than 100-fold between observations (explosive dynamics over a long gap), compute its gradient in forward mode as a cross-check. The default reverse mode is accurate there too. The first such subject in a session compiles the filter again, which takes minutes for a large model. fit$optim$explosive_passes counts such subjects, and the fit warns when any is explosive at the estimate.

lbfgs_diagonal

Julia. Default TRUE. L-BFGS learns a separate scale for each parameter from the curvature (Gilbert and Lemarechal). FALSE uses one scale for all, which can be much slower on large models. Like stochastic, it can take a fit further toward a degenerate limit.

lbfgs_gll

Julia. Default 0. A window W: a step is accepted if it improves on the worst of the last W objective values (Grippo, Lampariello and Lucidi), which lets the fit cross a curved valley.

lbfgs_nonmonotone

Julia. Between 0 (the default) and 1. A step is accepted against a running average of recent objective values (Zhang and Hager).

initial_alpha

Julia. Default 0.1. The length of the first trial step, in raw units.

lbfgs_growth

Julia. Default 2. In each optimisation that starts without curvature information, no step moves a parameter more than this many times the largest move that parameter has made so far (or a tenth of the largest move of any parameter, if that is larger). This keeps the first steps short while the rest of the model settles, which can stop factor loadings from changing sign early on. 0 removes the limit.

precondition

Julia. Default FALSE. TRUE sets L-BFGS's initial scaling of each parameter from the model's transforms, instead of learning it from the curvature. This can make fits whose intercepts start far from the data end in worse optima.

saem

Julia, intoverpop = 'laplace'. Default FALSE. Start with SAEM, which samples the random effects from their conditional distribution instead of integrating them with the Laplace approximation. The usual optimiser then finishes on the Laplace objective, so the estimate is usually the same as without SAEM, but SAEM can lead to a different maximum when the objective has more than one. Because SAEM's result has Monte Carlo error, the fit also runs once from its usual start without SAEM, and keeps the maximum with the higher log posterior after the Laplace approximation is corrected by quadrature. fit$optim$saem_guard records both. For a more accurate estimate than the Laplace approximation gives, sample with optimize = FALSE. A number sets the maximum number of SAEM iterations (TRUE is 10000). fit$optim$saem_iterations, saem_settled, saem_trend, saem_chains, saem_acceptance and saem_trace record the SAEM run.

saem_proposal

Julia. SAEM's proposal, 'rw' or 'laplace'.

restarts

Julia. Default 0. The number of random restarts for a fit that has not converged after its other corrections, typically because the likelihood has more than one maximum. Each starts from the fit's own start plus normal noise with sd restartsd (default 1) on the raw scale, and the best result is kept. Restarts run in worker processes when cores > 1 and the fit took more than 30 seconds. Not used when inits or maxiter were supplied. fit$optim$restarts records each start.

Newton steps and convergence checks (julia)

newton

Default TRUE. Take Newton steps near the maximum, with the exact Hessian, updated after each step and computed again when progress slows. The Hessian at the end is used for the convergence check and the standard errors. The steps also move away from a saddle point along the direction of negative curvature, and test directions with no curvature. With intoverpop = 'laplace' they run only when the fit is certified (certify). The value may name the curvature the steps use: 'chord' (the default except as below), 'exact' (a new Hessian whenever a step makes slow progress), 'subset', or 'krylov' (the outer product of the subjects' scores, corrected by Hessian-vector products at each step, with the exact Hessian computed at the end). 'krylov' is the default with intoverpop = 'laplace' when the exact Hessian would cost at least 200 gradients. fit$optim$newton_steps records the steps, and newton_krylov_products the gradients the Krylov steps used.

certify

Default TRUE. Check from the curvature that the fit has converged. estonly also skips it.

gaptol

Default 5e-5. The fit continues while the curvature at the estimate predicts more than this gain in the objective. The default corresponds to 0.01 standard errors from the maximum, close enough that the Hessian at the estimate is the Hessian at the maximum. A smaller value, such as 1e-6, holds the estimate closer still.

hessianreuse

Default 0.3. How far, in standard errors, the estimate may be from where a Hessian was computed for that Hessian still to give the standard errors. A Hessian from this far away adds roughly this fraction to the error of the standard errors. Computing a new one costs a gradient per parameter, or two with intoverpop = 'laplace'. 0 always computes it at the estimate.

innergaptol

The gain that a less reliable prediction (from L-BFGS, or from a Newton step on a Hessian computed elsewhere) must fall below for the fit to stop. By default a hundredth of gaptol. A gain predicted by the exact Hessian at the estimate is compared with gaptol itself.

overshoot

'magnitude' (the default), 'saturation' or 'off'. Which directions are pulled back after a fit, to test whether it stopped at a maximum.

stallwindow, stallratio, stallcooldown

The stall check (defaults 80, 0.001 and 30). The number of iterations over which a fit's gain is measured (a gain of half a unit of log likelihood or less starts a search for a transform that has gone flat), how much of its responsiveness a transform must have lost to count as the reason the fit stopped, and how many iterations the check waits after finding a fit slow but not stuck.

escapepin

Default FALSE. When the optimiser restarts from a point where it pulled some parameters back, hold those parameters fixed while the others are optimised, then free them. The flatretry restart always does this.

Laplace approximation (julia, intoverpop = 'laplace')

laplace_inner_maxiter, laplace_inner_tol

Defaults 200 and 1e-10. Iteration limit and tolerance for finding each subject's (or group's) random-effect mode. Raise the first when the fit reports modes that did not converge. The tolerance applies to the gradient, and is at least 1e-10 * (1 + abs(value)).

laplace_onestep

FALSE (the default) or TRUE. Where the Kalman filter can integrate a subject's random effects on initial means, intercepts or predictor effects exactly, given the subject's other random effects, it does, and the Laplace approximation covers only the others. TRUE uses one Laplace approximation over all of them instead. With random dynamics (a random drift or diffusion) the default is more accurate. Models whose dynamics depend on the state always use the single approximation, and ctModelImprove() and ctScoreTest() use it too when comparing such a model with one that does not.

laplace_soft_directions

'quadrature' (the default) or 'logdet_floor'. How to integrate a subject's random effects in a direction where their posterior is flatter than the prior, where the plain Laplace approximation overstates the likelihood. 'quadrature' integrates the flattest direction with a three-point quadrature when the curvature has an eigenvalue below 0.7, blending into plain Laplace between 0.2 and 0.7. 'logdet_floor' floors the log determinant at zero. Recorded in fit$laplace$soft_directions and used by every function that rebuilds the objective, and fit$laplace$conditioning counts such subjects. Also applies when sampling with intoverpop = FALSE and sampleControl$placement = 'fit'.

Uncertainty

uncertainty

Both. Default 'hessian' ('sandwich' with subject weights on julia). The uncertainty method computed when the optimiser ends, as in ctFitUncertainty. The default is meant for building a model, with the checks below. For intervals to report, sample with ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample'). 'sample' is not accepted here. Use optimize = FALSE, or ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') after the fit.

checks

Julia. Default TRUE, which runs the checks below, as the checks argument of ctFitUncertainty does. FALSE runs none, and any of 'randomeffects', 'intervals' and 'maximum' runs those named. The first two do not run with estonly. The random-effects check (with intoverpop = 'laplace') scores the Laplace approximation for every subject at draws of its random effects, and warns if integrating them exactly would move an estimate by 0.1 standard errors or more. The warning gives the size of the move when it is below one standard error, and how far the Laplace log likelihood is from the integrated one, and points to ctFitUncertainty(fit, intoverpop = 'quadrature') and to sampling. When the check runs, fit$estimate$loglik is the Laplace log likelihood corrected by the check, with loglik_se its standard error, loglik_laplace the uncorrected value, and loglik_method 'checked'. Models whose random effects enter linearly pass at once. If the optimiser stopped where the Laplace approximation for some subjects jumps, the fit warns instead and names them. fit$laplace$correction records the check. With optimize = FALSE, sampling the joint posterior, the check is made on the fit that places the chains, and where it finds a move of a standard error or more that fit is refined by quadrature and the chains start at the refined estimate. The interval check (with uncertainty = 'hessian') tests whether the normal approximation from the Hessian matches the posterior, and says so in a message and in summary() where it does not. With intoverpop = 'quadrature' it uses the refined fit, and can then take longer than the refinement. checks = 'randomeffects' leaves it out. The maximum check (with optimize = FALSE, sampling the joint posterior) looks at where the sampler's first draws are centred. If that is far from the estimate it optimises from there, and if this reaches a higher log posterior the model is fitted again from that point before sampling. fit$sample$maximumcheck records the check.

uncertaintyDraws, finishsamples, uncertaintyControl

Both. The draws argument of ctOptimUncertainty (default 'auto'), and the finishsamples (1000) and control arguments of ctFitUncertainty.

accuracy, sampleControl

Julia. A target accuracy in posterior standard deviations, off by default. After the uncertainty method has run, its estimate of its own error is compared with this, and if it falls short, or gives none, the fit is sampled to that accuracy (control$accuracy in ctFitUncertainty). sampleControl holds the other sampler settings for that run.

estonly

Both. Default FALSE. Point estimates only, without a Hessian, so there are no standard errors and no convergence check. With intoverpop = 'laplace' there are also no Newton steps and no random-effects check.

Progress and output (julia)

callback

A function called while the fit runs, with arguments (iteration, total, objective, gradient_norm, parameters), where parameters is the raw parameter vector. A function with only the first four arguments is called with four. It is called at regular time intervals and once at the end, for example to show progress in a front end. An error inside it disables it, with a warning. fit$optim$trace holds every iteration after the fit, and ctTracePlot plots it. To save a checkpoint to resume from, use checkpoint.

checkpoint

A file path. While the fit optimises, its current point is saved there every checkpoint_every seconds (default 60) and at the end of each stage, together with the random-effect modes (with intoverpop = 'laplace') and the smoothing parameters of any smooth terms. Each exact Hessian the fit computes is saved beside it (<checkpoint>.hessian). If the file already exists, the fit starts from it, so running the same call again resumes an interrupted fit, including its modes, smoothing parameters and Hessian. A file written for a different model stops the fit instead of being overwritten.

progress

Force the progress line on or off.

tipredMissing

How missing values of time independent predictors are handled. Each missing value gets a normal distribution from a regression on the other variables. 'impute' sets it to the mean of that distribution, 'sample' treats it as a parameter with that distribution as its prior, and 'auto', the default, imputes when optimizing and samples when sampling. ctFitUncertainty(fit, 'sample') uses the fit's setting, and its control$tipredMissing overrides it.

tipredMissingIncludeOutcome

Default TRUE. Whether the outcome informs the imputation of missing TI predictors.

saveEffects

A sampling setting, read here for older scripts. Use sampleControl$saveEffects.

Stan only

nsubsets, subsamplesize, lproughnesstarget, stochasticTolAdjust, parsteps

Tuning of stan's stochastic-gradient optimiser and its stepwise phase.

stalltol

Default 0.01. The gradient per data point above which stan calls a fit stalled and restarts it (see stallretries).

See also

ctFit, ctFitUncertainty, ctTracePlot.
